A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same work, Epistemic Monte Carlo Tree Search. All 27 pages, including Appendices A–F, are readable, and their text, equations, figures, and tables support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v5 reports original subleq and Deep Sea experiments in Section 5, with additional exploration analyses and MinAtar results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v6 retains those original experiments and results in Section 5 and Appendix C, including Figures 1–5 and Table 1.

M1.justification: The epistemic search policies, uncertainty propagation, and EMCTS procedure in Section 3 and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The objectives, losses, and implementation variants in the appendices also match.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same subleq tasks, deterministic- and stochastic-reward Deep Sea scenarios, and four MinAtar games. No dataset, task, or evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within each experiment: AZ in the subleq and MinAtar comparisons, and the corresponding A/MZ, A/MZ+UBE, and Bootstrapped DQN comparisons in the Deep Sea figures and table.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, environments, training budgets, model configurations, and testing procedures match throughout Section 5 and Appendices C–F. For example, both retain 50 MCTS simulations for Deep Sea and 32 for subleq.

E4.justification: Both retain the exploration-parameter sensitivity analysis in Figure 2, uncertainty-estimation visualization in Figure 3, and exploration-rate and transition-model comparisons in Figure 4. No ablation or supplementary analysis is added or revised.

E5.justification: Run counts and uncertainty-reporting practices are identical. Figure 1 retains 15 seeds and two standard errors; Figure 2 and Appendix C retain their respective seed counts, standard errors, and Table 1 standard deviations.

E6.justification: Figures 1–5 and Table 1 retain the same results, curves, and rankings. For example, Table 1 reports 10,539 ± 9,006 steps for E-AZ and 22,801 ± 7,514 for AZ+UBE with RND in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, Theorem 1, Appendix A proofs and variance-bound derivation, and Appendix B treatment of learned transition dynamics are unchanged. Minor extraction-spacing differences do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about uncertainty-aware MCTS, deep exploration, and improved sample efficiency. Their scientific scope and strength are unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of search-based uncertainty estimation and exploration remain identical. The qualifications concerning independence assumptions, learned transition models, and reliable novelty estimation are also retained without revision.

D1.justification: The subleq specification, Deep Sea implementation details, network architectures, and hyperparameters in Appendices D–F match. The implementation link and code-related access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 4, the bibliography, and discussions positioning EMCTS relative to prior search and uncertainty-estimation methods are unchanged. No cited work is added or removed.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v5, 2 April 2025, to v6, 15 May 2026. The paper's prose, headings, section order, and appendix organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–5, Tables 1–4, and Algorithm 1 retain their displays, captions, and placement. Figure geometry and embedded images match; tiny glyph-position differences do not constitute a layout revision.

improvement.justification: v6 preserves the same methods, proofs, empirical evidence, interpretations, and reproducibility information throughout the main text and appendices. The updated version stamp and negligible rendering differences provide no meaningful improvement or deterioration in paper quality.
